Just because a brand is everywhere in our daily routine doesn’t mean we rush to buy its shares on day one.

With all the buzz around the upcoming Jio IPO, it’s easy to think: “Everyone uses it, so it must be a great investment!” But being a loyal customer is very different from being an investor.

Before putting your hard-earned money in, pause and ask:

👉🏼 What am I buying beyond the main brand? (Broadband, apps, cloud?)

👉🏼 Is future growth already priced too high?

👉🏼 What could go wrong? (Competition, rising costs, tech shifts)

👉🏼 Does this actually fit my personal financial plan?

👉🏼 An IPO isn’t an obligation to buy. It’s an invitation to do your homework quietly, at your own pace ☕

Save this checklist for the next headline, and tell us: what’s the first question you ask before investing? 💛

A passionate educator and financial literacy advocate, Hiral founded Investing for Mummies with a mission to make money and investing simple, accessible, and less intimidating for beginners.

As the featured voice in this edition of Her Trail, Her Tale, Hiral shares her journey of empowering women to take charge of their finances, build confidence with money, and make informed financial decisions.

The best part of teaching finance isn’t hearing, “I understand investing now.”

It’s hearing:
“I feel confident enough to be part of the conversation.”

From understanding financial terms to having a voice in family money decisions, every message like this reminds us why Investing for Mummies began.

To every woman who walked into our workshops with curiosity, questions and the willingness to learn, thank you for trusting us to be part of your journey.

We’re grateful to be learning, growing and making money conversations feel a little easier, together.

You don’t need to manage every investment or understand every financial term. But knowing where your family’s money is, how it’s invested, and being part of the decisions that shape your future matters.

This Women’s Equality Day, start with one conversation. Financial confidence can follow.

What happens in Jackson Hole can move markets far beyond Wyoming. 🏔️

The key investing lesson? Markets don’t just react to what’s happening today, they’re constantly trying to anticipate what comes next.

A few words from central bankers can influence expectations around interest rates, inflation, currencies, gold and even Indian markets.
